findings.problem: At [1:61] Holmes has only read her index entry and summarised the King's entanglement and compromising letters. The snapshot already says the affair happened when he was Crown Prince (revealed [1:80]) and that she has a photograph (first raised [1:74], 'both in the photograph' [1:76]).
findings.evidence: [1:61] 'Your Majesty, as I understand, became entangled with this young person, wrote her some compromising letters, and is now desirous of getting those letters back.' / [1:80] 'I was only Crown Prince then.' / [1:76] 'We were both in the photograph.'
findings.fix: Replace the [1:61] body with: 'An American-born contralto, born in New Jersey in 1858, once prima donna of the Imperial Opera of Warsaw and now retired and living in London. The King of Bohemia, who calls her a well-known adventuress, met her in Warsaw some five years ago, became entangled with her, and wants back the compromising letters he wrote her.' (Alternatively keep the current text and move the gate to [1:80].)

findings.problem: The first card appears at 'I am the King' [1:55], but it gives his age (stated at [1:80]) and says he came from Prague incognito (stated at [1:57]).
findings.evidence: [1:57] 'I have come incognito from Prague for the purpose of consulting you.' / [1:80] 'I am but thirty now.'
findings.fix: Replace the [1:55] body with: 'The hereditary King of Bohemia, of the House of Ormstein. He is the masked visitor who called himself Count Von Kramm, and he has just torn off his mask and admitted who he is.' Thirty and Prague are already in the [1:102] snapshot.

findings.problem: The [1:55] snapshot says he goes on using the name while staying at the Langham. The text gives that at [1:104].
findings.evidence: [1:104] 'You will find me at the Langham under the name of the Count Von Kramm.'
findings.fix: Replace the [1:55] body with: 'A false name. The masked visitor who called himself Count Von Kramm, a Bohemian nobleman, is the King of Bohemia himself. He tears off his mask after Holmes addresses him as ‘your Majesty’.' Optionally add a [1:104] snapshot that appends: 'He goes on using the name while staying at the Langham.'

findings.problem: The thread calls him 'young'. The text never gives his age; he is described as dark, handsome, dashing, aquiline and moustached.
findings.evidence: [1:129] 'He is dark, handsome, and dashing, never calls less than once a day, and often twice.' / [1:132] 'a remarkably handsome man, dark, aquiline, and moustached'
findings.fix: Thread: 'A dark, handsome lawyer of the Inner Temple who calls at Briony Lodge at least once a day.'

findings.problem: 'coldly ignores the King’s outstretched hand' turns Watson's neutral wording ('without observing') into a narrator-certified snub. 'Coldly' belongs to Holmes's remark at [1:248], not to the bow.
findings.evidence: [1:257] 'He bowed, and, turning away without observing the hand which the King had stretched out to him, he set off in my company for his chambers.'
findings.fix: Replace the last sentence with: 'He gives Holmes her portrait as a reward; Holmes takes it, bows, and turns away without taking the King’s outstretched hand.'

findings.problem: The cast list appears when the story opens. Together, its entries give away the opening mystery (who the masked visitor is and what he wants, [1:41]-[1:98]). The King's thread says he needs Holmes to recover a compromising photograph. The Count's thread describes a masked Bohemian visitor. Irene's thread says she holds a photograph a powerful man wants and will not sell (the refusal is at [1:84]). This reveals the setup rather than the outcome, so it is minor.
findings.evidence: [1:55] 'I am the King. Why should I attempt to conceal it?' / [1:84] 'She will not sell.'
findings.fix: King thread: 'The hereditary King of Bohemia, of the House of Ormstein, whose private affairs are at stake in this story.' Irene thread: 'A retired opera singer, born in America and now living quietly at Briony Lodge in St. John’s Wood. To Holmes she is always ‘the woman’.' Keep the Count thread as is.
